string.text: Greetings, Professor. I got a question for you - what do you know about the Phantasm?

Ah, the Phantasm - specimen LGC-2307, "Polypus volans terribilis"! A most fascinating subject, and yes, we do have some data compiled on it. But I'm curious - what's prompted your interest in this particular organism?
Well, I must find and kill it.
Kill it? Ha - well, I'll be direct with you. You're hardly the first to set that goal for themselves!
What can you tell me about it? What exactly are we dealing with here? I'm guessing this isn't some run-of-the-mill mutant you can just put down with a full magazine at close range?

Ah, now you're asking the right questions! Let's say this specimen is remarkably interesting - it possesses, shall we say, extrasensory perception of a sort. It's capable of generating phantom objects and formations of an energy-informational, or perhaps ectoplasmic, nature. And the way it levitates - quite extraordinary, indeed! \n \nWere we ever granted the chance to observe it again, our understanding of psychotronic phenomena would advance considerably. And if we could obtain a specimen for dissection... well, the possibilities would be remarkable indeed.
Wait, you've encountered it before?

We maintained a modest field camp out in the swamps, dedicated in part to observing specimen 2307. There's nothing there now, I'm afraid - the entire staff appears to have vanished into thin air, quite without explanation...
So how do I defeat it, then?

I won't sugarcoat it for you - your odds aren't favorable. The creature spends the majority of its time submerged, and it's not the sort of thing that simply emerges on a whim. \n \nThat said, we do possess an apparatus calibrated to emit signals at frequencies to which it's notably sensitive. I'd wager that, with its use, you could lure the Phantasm to the surface.
Great. What do you want for it in return?
My, a born dealmaker! Very well - given your evident enthusiasm for eliminating LGC-2307, I daresay you'd have no objection to dealing with a few other specimens for us as well, hm?
What are you getting at?

You've surely been to Bright Beam before and know the surrounding area well. Our expeditions there have reported sightings of a similar creature in the marshy lowlands beyond the town. 
 
Based on the data we've gathered, it's quite clear this isn't LGC-2307 itself, but rather a distinct, if related, organism - one with considerably more limited psychotronic capabilities. 
 
And since proper study of the "Phantasm" remains out of reach given the extreme danger it poses, I propose, young man, that you... eliminate this lesser specimen instead. Our research team will handle the rest from there. Don't trouble yourself - we'll provide you with an experimental psi-blocker prototype, along with a "lure" device.
Hold on, hold on! So in order to get the gear I need to hunt this monstrosity, you're telling me I first have to kill... a different monstrosity?!

Precisely, yes. You assist us in retrieving the specimen's body from Bright Beam, and in exchange we'll furnish you with a second equipment set for dealing with your Phantasm. \n \nIt also presents a convenient opportunity to field-test the device under genuine conditions.
Fine. So what's my best bet weapon-wise against it?

Ah, splendid that you asked! The difficulty, you see, is that ordinary bullets seem to have virtually no effect on it. Something with considerably more punch - explosives, say - stands a far better chance. \n \nOur expedition team, in fact, managed to repel the creature on one occasion with nothing more than a pair of well-aimed grenades.
Here's your equipment, Professor.
Splendid! Do tell me you avoided drawing attention in the village, hm?
No, I didn't. Though why all the cloak and dagger stuff? Aren't those just regular bandits in there - just better armed?
Suffice it to say, the finer details are best left unexamined, for your own sake. You've fulfilled your end of things, so let's proceed with our discussion.
Hooah, we made it!
Well, well - the Zone really rolled out the red carpet for you...

Don't even get me started, man... If it weren't for you, we'd be done for. And where the hell did those thugs get rockets from? Absolutely insane! 
 
Alright, here's the cargo - needs to go to the Professor. Old man's probably losing his patience, been living off army rations for a week now. 
 
Thanks again, seriously!
Yeah, well... take care out there!
Anything else?

I take it you're aware we're among the very few scientific outfits permitted to operate within the Zone officially? No? Well, you are now... \n \nAnd, as is so often the case with government-funded endeavors, we find ourselves perpetually wanting - for everything, really, from basic supplies to research instrumentation. A few hours past, we submitted a request to the Mainland for some necessary equipment. Air delivery remains the only feasible option.
Go on, Professor. What needs to be done?

All that's asked of you is to ensure the helicopter arrives safely. You see, the local marauders have developed a rather inconvenient habit of ambushing our supply runs as of late. Given the anomalous activity originating from beneath the lake, our pilots must fly at a low altitude, leaving them precious little room to maneuver - or to respond - should they come under attack. 
 
Head toward the abandoned village and oversee the cargo's arrival. I'd suggest keeping a low profile - perhaps take up a position on one of the rooftops, out of sight. Once the helicopter touches down, collect the delivery from the pilot and bring it back to our bunker. 
 
Here - take this rifle, for whatever circumstances might arise... Though I'll trust you to return it once the matter's been resolved.
Professor, I've been to the laboratory under Dark Valley...
What- you've seen something of interest down there? Surely you don't mean to tell me you've found something?!
A handful of bodies, deceased. From the look of things, your personnel. They were carrying some kind of device - here, see for yourself...

Oh, how dreadful... I shall be far more careful before sending anyone underground without an escort again. They were fine men, dedicated to their work - this is a genuine loss, and they deserved better. May they rest in peace. \n \nNow then - do hand over whatever you've found. And as a small token of gratitude for such a discovery, please accept this from me.
Ah, you've come across something more, have you? Do go on then - let's see what you've brought.
Greetings, Professor.

My dear fellow, you have no idea the debt the scientific community now owes you! With this, we can finally push deeper into the Zone without dreading a psychotronic surge catching us unawares. \n \nGood lord, how many years we've hoped for precisely this! Our laboratory's funding is all but guaranteed to grow now. You have my deepest, most sincere thanks.
Anytime! Though, truth be told, gratitude doesn't exactly pay the bills out here. I was rather hoping for something a touch more... material.
Oh, trust me, I understand. Here you go. You deserve it.

Good heavens! Is our mobile laboratory under attack once more? Blast it all, the defense grid has gone offline! \n \nThis has to be more zombies - they've slipped beyond the installation's control. And unless I'm mistaken, they're advancing toward us as we speak!
Well, I'd better get go-...
Good lord, don't just stand there! Run to the head of security, he'll tell you what's needed. \n \nAnd yes, you'll be compensated handsomely for this, as ever. Now go, quickly!
Professor, are you alright? The zombies have been dealt with...
Yes, I do believe I'm quite alright. One does wonder where they keep coming from... Though no matter, this is far from our first such incident. And you - are you unharmed?
I'm fine, I think... My guess is a controller brought them here, possibly from the city.
At any rate, they won't be bothering us again. Do take this as a token of our gratitude - I daresay you'll find it rather useful.
Professor, what can you tell me about the mutants that inhabit the Zone?

Certainly! Though I must be transparent with you, young man - biology is rather outside my area of expertise, so my knowledge here is admittedly limited. I certainly couldn't speak authoritatively on every creature the Zone has seen fit to produce. \n \nThat said, I shall endeavor to answer whatever I can. So - which particular specimens have caught your interest?
I'd like to know about Controllers.
I'd like to know more about Zombies.
Burers. I'd like to hear about Burers.
What can you tell me about Pseudogiants?
What about Pseudodogs? Or dogs in general, really.

A great many theories surround their origins. The most widely accepted posits that they are the unfortunate remnants of a failed experiment in human neurological manipulation. They are exceptionally dangerous - capable of subjugating a victim through sustained eye contact alone. An open encounter with one is, for all practical purposes, a near-certain death.

They are particularly prevalent here at Yantar, I'm afraid. What you see is merely a shell - what remains of a person following sustained exposure to psi-radiation. In the earlier stages of deterioration, some retain the motor capacity to operate weapons, which makes them decidedly dangerous at that juncture. \n \nIn more advanced stages, they are little more than ambulatory corpses. A sizeable group of them, however, presents a challenge that shouldn't be underestimated at any stage of deterioration.

Their origins remain something of a mystery, though the evidence suggests a process not entirely dissimilar to the experiments behind the controllers. They possess notable kinetic capabilities - able to interact with and manipulate objects at considerable distance. Remarkably dangerous specimens, and ones that tend to confine themselves to subterranean environments.

They are, arguably, among the most formidable specimens the Zone has produced. Their sheer physical scale is enough to unsettle even the most hardened of stalkers, and one frequently encounters individuals whose hide proves entirely impervious to automatic rifle fire. Cognitively, they are quite primitive - lumbering masses driven by nothing more than raw instinct.

Most dogs out here are simply canis lupus familiaris - ordinary domestic animals, modestly changed by anomalous conditions. Curiously, nearly all were once purebreds. My hypothesis is that blind dogs originated somewhere underground, products of the Zone's accelerated evolutionary processes, before surfacing and displacing the common strays entirely. 
 
Pseudodogs are another matter altogether. Consensus points to modified wolves, though the debate over mutation versus distinct species shows no sign of settling. Remarkable creatures - the jaw structure alone, unfolding not unlike certain fish species, with a skeleton far closer to felines than canines. Kovalenko nearly lost his mind with excitement when our first specimen came in for dissection, heh. 
 
What sets them apart most, however, is their psionic ability - used in hunting and in commanding other animals. They transmit thought-images to blind dog packs, acting as collective "eyes" and issuing simple telepathic orders. A crude but effective analogue to the Controller. 
 
Exercise caution, young man. There are credible reports of Pseudodogs affecting humans as well - especially those severely intoxicated or physically exhausted.
Actually, never mind.
Thank you for the information, Professor!
I have a few more questions, actually.
Here's your payment. Is there anything else you need?
No.
I've brought something for you.
Excellent! What have you got there?
A "Magnet".
A strong gravitational artifact.
A "Double Empty".
A "Black Droplets".
A "Electric Ball".
A "Mercury Ball".
A "Sponge".
A "Empty".
A "Dead Head".
A "Needles".
A "Strong needles".
Maybe another time.
What exactly is going on here?

We are engaged in the scientific study of the Zone's phenomena. Though I'll admit, the more time passes, the more I wonder whether such a thing is truly achievable. Regardless, you could be of considerable assistance to us by procuring a few anomalous formations - artifacts, as they're commonly known.
So I should just bring you whatever I come across?

Not at all - common artifacts are entirely beneath our interest. We have need only of the rarest specimens available. Should you procure something suitable, we'll buy it from you regardless of condition for a fixed sum of five hundred dollars.
Excellent. I will return with artifacts on hand, then.
The container's been delivered.
Wonderful. Did they receive you?
Yeah, there was a guy waiting for me. Got it sorted. By the way, what's the deal with that village - anyone actually live there, or is it just another abandoned spot?

Workers from this complex once lived there, children included. From what I've heard, they all disappeared at once - just like that. A troubling affair with no clear explanation... and curiously, something very similar was reported around the Bar, where residential buildings were also inhabited at the time...
I know that much already. Can you tell me anything about the Journalist?

A stalker like most others, though admittedly something of an oddity. I don't know a great deal about him personally, but he was a frequent presence at the Bar - always seeking out some piece of information or another. \n \nI also know with some certainty that he spent a period of time around the ruins of a house here at Yantar, and made a habit of combing through Bright Beam as well. If you're attempting to trace his movements, I'd suggest beginning there. I'm afraid that's the extent of what I can offer you.
Understood. The Bar and Yantar it is then - that gives me somewhere to start at least.
Once again, my thanks, Messer.
So what's this work about? Professor sent me your way...
You know how to drive? Never mind, I can see from the look of you that you do - you're no rookie. Listen, I need a vehicle with a container driven out to the village.
What kind of vehicle are we talking about?

Just an old RAF van with a sideboard flatbed, sitting right here at the base. We use the thing to cart around all sorts of junk... Here's the key. Drop the container off and leave the rig there - someone will come collect it and move it where it needs to go.
Is anyone going to be there to meet me?
Yes, someone will be there to meet you. We work closely with a lot of regular stalkers... you're not the only one we deal with.
Good.
And take it easy on the road - last thing we need is the cargo bouncing out the back!
All good, Professor - the measurements have been taken.
Ah yes, indeed! The results have come through. n\ \nVery good, Messer!
So what's next?

The picture is coming together rather nicely, young man! There are indeed subterranean structures beneath the central complex by the lake - and it is from these that the signal originates, the very one generating the "barrier" that acts upon the human mind. \n \nIn principle, one could reach the source and deactivate it. The difficulty, however, is that every access point is presently blocked by concentrated psychotronic radiation. That said, working from the data you've provided, I've managed to construct a shielding blocker - one that should allow you to make your way underground.
You're suggesting I find the source of the signal and destroy it?

Precisely so. Or at minimum, deactivate it should outright destruction prove unfeasible. Here, take the radiation blocker! \n \nOur best estimate places the entrance inside the large hangar near the collapsed loading bridge. Beyond that, I'm afraid we have no intelligence on what may be inside. So I implore you, Messer - please exercise the utmost caution in there.
I'll do my best.
Splendid. I have every confidence in you, Messer!
Rat said you're the one to talk to about getting to the Center.

Yes, the Barkeep contacted us to go over the current situation. Unlikely as it may sound, our goals align more than one might expect - and in principle, assisting you in reaching the Center is something we could attempt. That said, I must be candid with you - it will be a great deal more difficult than it appears on the surface.
So what exactly do you need me to do?

I suspect you're already aware that the Zone has a rather alarming effect on the human mind. The further north one ventures, the greater the likelihood of complete psychological burnout - what stalkers have come to call "shells," or Zombies. The psychotronic radiation responsible for this, however, manifests in weaker concentrations elsewhere throughout the Zone as well. 
 
Were we able to identify these secondary sources and understand their operating principles, we'd be in a position to construct a shielding device capable of protecting its user on the approach to the northern territories. 
 
We've sent out expeditions to collect intelligence on potential signal sources - none of which have returned, I'm sorry to say. Of particular concern is the fact that they carried prototype psychotronic shielding devices, which we must recover in order to obtain the readings necessary for developing a new prototype. 
 
The expedition was last reported sheltering in an apartment in the northern part of Bright Beam. The Freedom faction leader will be able to tell you more precisely - he maintained contact with them up until the moment of their disappearance. 
 
Additionally, our research requires two samples of gravitational weaponry. I shan't mislead you - acquiring them will be no simple matter. That said, there are credible accounts among stalkers of creatures in the Dark Valley underground, armed with devices of exactly this nature - crude constructions of scrap and artifacts.
Alright, we have a deal. I'll track down the prototypes and look into the gravitational weapons while I'm at it.

Splendid, Messer! There is one additional matter - documentation pertaining to the operating principles of psychotronic radiation. Shall we say, we have considerable grounds to believe the Agroprom Research Institute once conducted research into the influence of human consciousness, the findings of which would be of tremendous value to our work. 
 
Whether any of it remains accessible is, I confess, uncertain. With any luck it hasn't been exported to the mainland as yet - I'd recommend enquiring with middleman traders or others who deal in the acquisition of information. They may be your best avenue there. 
 
Oh, and do pay a visit to the Clear Sky leader - I'm quite confident he'll have something of relevance for you.
Consider it done. I'll start asking around.
Wonderful. You may begin at your earliest convenience. Once the matter is concluded, we shall reconvene and determine how best to proceed from there.
Professor. I've got everything you asked for.
Ah, Messer! Do hand them over at once - let's see what we have to work with here...
Well, what do you make of it?

Quite intriguing, I must say. Regrettably, the data contained here will need to be decrypted before it's of any use to us. And before we can advance to the next stage of our research, psychotronic field readings will need to be taken.
And what exactly does that have to do with me? I'm no scientist - I don't know a thing about taking readings!

Not to worry, young man - your role is simply to escort one of our colleagues, who will handle the readings himself. He ought to be returning from his latest excursion shortly. Make your way to the parking area exit and you should see him - he'll be approaching from the direction of the grounded barge.
I'll head that way, then.

Do exercise caution out there - mutant activity has been observed in that vicinity! 
 
Oh, and before it slips my mind - please, accept this as a small expression of our gratitude. It's a power cell for an exoskeleton, enabling the equipment to function at full capacity. I must stress, however, that these are extraordinarily rare - the likelihood of finding another functional unit anywhere in the Zone is rather slim. Treat it accordingly. It can be recharged here in our bunker whenever necessary. 
 
Now - off you go. The assistant should be arriving at the bunker quite soon.
You're the one taking the psi-field readings?
That's me. Here's the plan: we move toward the tower by the village, then move to the left side of the parking lot, then on to the bunker and the dome. Once everything's done, we head back to base.
Got it.
Oh, and look - reinforcements for the camp are on their way. It looks like the Professor pulled it off with the local stalkers. Good to know. Alright, enough standing around - let's get going!
Professor, do you got any water on you?
Why, certainly! There's a kettle of water right behind you. Help yourself - drink until you can't drink anymore!
I see, how much for a cup?
For you? On the house. Go right ahead!
Hey there. Who are you?

We're Clear Sky. Think of us as the environmentalists of the stalker world. We study the Zone, searching for a way to cure the world of this affliction. We don't take sides with any other faction - we're strictly neutral.
Got it. I take it you're working alongside the eggheads?
That's right. Unfortunately, we're a small group - not many people see things the way we do.
You going to the base? Visiting the scientists? Alright, go on through. Just keep that shooter holstered!
So, what, you're the protector of the eggheads now?
Yep. It pays well enough, and there isn't much to it. Mostly just chasing off the odd zombie or a stalker who's had one too many.
Sounds like you've got it handled. I'll let you get back to it.
Messer! You really pulled it off! Heavens, I scarcely know where to begin... the radiation has stopped completely. I daresay it's time we considered pushing north.
Hey there. Yeah, that wasn't a walk in the park. So you're thinking of heading north? What do you say we join forces?

No, regrettably, that particular road isn't one I'm meant to walk... though I daresay our paths may cross again before all is said and done. My thanks once more, Messer, for all you've done in service of this work!
Good luck to you!

Just for you, we'll offer a substantial discount - two thousand even. What do you say? Just keep in mind, after the treatment your system will be highly susceptible to spores, so I'd recommend staying away from any sources of infection for a while until your immunity recovers.

Compose yourself! You should consider yourself fortunate that disabling that wretched installation happens to align with our own interests. Take the helmet - though I'll have no discussion of payment, given how thoroughly you've botched this, young man. 
 
The entrance to the underground complex lies within the large loading hangar; that is your way down. Whatever you do, avoid the center of the complex - the radiation levels there remain entirely off the charts. 
 
Now go. And don't think of returning empty-handed.
Do you have a job?

A week ago, a group of scientists went into town to make observations and disappeared. It's hard to say what could have happened to them. The city's crawling with zombies and whatnot. Besides, our people aren't very good fighters. We don't have anyone to search for them. We need to find the scientists or their corpses and find the results of the observations, if there are any.
Alright, I'll try to find them.
Anything you find, bring it back here to the bunker.
